decisions.reason: The downward pour direction is owned by the spout-orientation Requirement and is consistent with the existing rendering-reference design; it does not change the candidate's appearance, material, or fabrication attributes.
The source selects a spout orientation intended to preserve drink consistency but does not change the existing controlled-pour or beverage-preservation acceptance criteria.
Changing the physical pour direction does not alter the solenoid actuation mechanism or press-and-release control behavior.
The source does not change the requirement for seals to prevent liquid from leaking into the base.
The spout's downward pour direction does not affect the placard's text, position, display sides, or viewing orientation.
The orientation change does not alter whether the spout is removable for cleaning.
The source does not change the bottom-bowl seal or its electrical-isolation function.
Directing the pour downward does not change the requirement that the spout support removal or flushing for effective cleaning.
The reference to preserving drink consistency concerns dispensing orientation and does not change the independently defined mixing or frothing output requirements.
The source does not establish a new splash-control target or modify any existing splash-mitigation behavior.
Spout pour direction has no entailed effect on the selected whisk design, material, or size requirements.
The mechanical spout-orientation decision does not change the specified electrical loads, power-supply headroom, or cooling requirements.
